#3314. AirPods 5 vs AirPods Pro 3: Which should you buy this holiday season?

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

AirPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:

The key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

If you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice …

AirPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

If you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $149. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

This year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

AirPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

If you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

Are you planning to buy anyone AirPods this holiday season? Are they on your wishlist? Let us know down in the comments.

It’s been a big year for audio releases, with major players like Apple, Beats, Bose, Sennheiser, and Sony all dropping new models. While a pair of flagship headphones can cost a premium, Black Friday deals are here. Many of the best headphones on the market are getting discounts, including models that were released just months ago.

Best of all, most of these Black Friday deals are on headphones we’ve tested, including our favorite travel headphones, styles for the gym, and noise-canceling cans. We’ve also included deals on wireless earbuds if you’re more partial to in-ear styles.

There are admittedly a lot of deals to sift through, so these are a few that are especially worth it:

You can check out the best Black Friday headphone and earbud deals below, organized by brand.

The Space 2 headphones are a great option if you’re looking for budget noise-canceling headphones, and they’re under $100.

In our testing, Anker’s Liberty 5 Pro earbuds lived up to the bold claim of delivering the best voice-calling performance, particularly in loud environments. They’re available for $130 during Black Friday.

The second-gen AirPods Max headphones impressed us with great noise-canceling and the most impressive transparency mode of any over-ear headphones. They’re pricey, but discounted right now.

Nothing’s over-ear headphones feature a quirky but stylish design, solid audio quality, and fun tactile controls. They’re $170 for Black Friday.

The Momentum 5 may be an upgrade over the fourth-gen model, but you’d be hard-pressed to find Bluetooth headphones that sound this good for this price.

#3308. The Best Tech Deals From Costco's Early Black Friday Sale

Sam's Club, Walmart, Amazon, and other retailers have been churning out early Black Friday deals since last week, so if you haven't been paying attention, you've already missed out on some good deals. But all hope is not lost: Costco recently started its own early sale, so you're still in time to find something you want at a low price. Below, I've rounded up my favorite tech deals from their sale—but keep in mind you'll need a membership to take advantage of these deals.

A powerful monitor with high-end specs can make gaming more immersive and greatly reduce input lag, which is helpful for any serious gamer looking for an edge over their opponents. The Samsung Odyssey G9 is a 49-inch gaming monitor with some impressive specs, including a 240Hz refresh rate and a 1 ms response time. It's available for $699.99 (originally $899.99), $200 off and the lowest price it has reached this year.

If you're looking for a more premium (and far more massive) gaming monitor, the 57-inch Samsung Odyssey Neo G9, one of the best ultra-wide gaming monitors on the market, is currently on sale for $1,449.99 ($2,499.99 at launch). This monitor came out in 2023, earning an "excellent" review from PCMag for its impressive 7,680 x 2,160 4K resolution, its great color range and accuracy, a 240Hz refresh rate, 1,000 nits of brightness, and its overall design. To make full use of its powerful 240Hz refresh rate, you'll need to use DisplayPort 2.1, or you'll be limited to 120Hz. You'll also need a powerful graphics card. The 15.3-inch Lenovo Legion is a powerful gaming laptop with premium specs, and with the current $600 discount, it's down to $1999.99 (originally $2,599.99). PCMag gave the more affordable 5i version an excellent review for its price and performance, so if you have the cash for it, this one is even better.

A soundbar is a great way to improve a home entertainment system without spending too much money. This 5.1 TCL Q6CH setup is currently $199.99 (originally $299.99), including a soundbar and subwoofer. This soundbar came out in 2024 and supports Dolby Atmos and DTS:X for that 3D sound, as well as AI Sonic, a tool that tunes your sound settings based on the setup of your room.

The latest AirPods Pro are a big step up from their previous generation. The third iteration of Apple's iconic earbuds deliver a number of quality-of-life and software improvements that make them worth the typical premium over the AirPods Pro 2—and right now, the AirPods Pro 3 are even cheaper than the previous generation: They're $179 at Costco (originally $249) in an early Black Friday deal.

The 15-inch MacBook Air is down to $1,249 (originally $1,499), the lowest price since Apple hiked prices this past summer. The M5 MacBook Air is the best laptop for most people looking for a new machine in 2026. In comparison to the already excellent M4 Air, the M5 base model has double the storage, and the powerful M5 chip makes the performance even smoother, according to Mashable's review. The aluminum design is as good as you'd expect from Apple's most popular portable laptop, and it includes a Liquid Retina display, Touch ID, a 12MP Center Stage Camera, and the Magic Keyboard.

The 15.6-inch Acer Aspire Go is a great value at its current $499.99 price (originally $699.99). The display is a touchscreen; it sports an AMD Ryzen 5 processor and it has 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. These aren't specs you normally find at this price, making it a great laptop for anyone looking to stretch their money as far as possible while getting a workhorse of a laptop.

I'm a fan of TCL TVs, and currently own the "non-pro" version of this TV. The 65-inch QM6K Pro is $599.99 (originally $999.99) and has the same internal hardware and Mini-LED panel as the regular QM6K, but it adds a CrystGlow anti-reflective coating that makes it more viewable in well-lit rooms and helps maintain a high picture contrast. The 144 Hz native refresh rate makes gaming smooth, and support for Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10+, HDR10, and HLG means you're well positioned to get the best sound quality when streaming movies or shows.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. #3307. Apple Watch Series 12: Four standout features make me glad I upgraded

I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip update, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

The new Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the new health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:

The complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a new Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

Most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

More battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off quickly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

Apple Watch Series 12 is now only $329 on Amazon, down from $399.

Have you upgraded to Apple Watch Series 12? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

#3305. Inside 2026 F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix: Celebrities, Late-Night Parties and Race-Day Drama

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

For the fourth year in a row, Formula 1 took over Las Vegas, transforming the Strip into a three-day collision of sport, nightlife, celebrity culture, and over-the-top entertainment.

The 2026 Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix arrived at the end of a banner season for the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team. Kimi Antonelli had already made history as Formula 1’s youngest-ever World Champion at 20 years old, while Mercedes secured its first Constructors’ Championship since 2021.

But two days before Antonelli and teammate George Russell raced through the streets of Las Vegas, they were competing in very different vehicles.

Organized by Marriott Bonvoy with Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team, the Fountains of Bellagio were transformed into a Formula 1-inspired racecourse, where the drivers and five Marriott Bonvoy members raced custom speedboats across the hotel’s famed waters. The event was part of Marriott Bonvoy Moments, which offers members access to exclusive experiences through the travel program’s longtime partners, including Mercedes (Marriott Bonvoy members can also currently bid on packages to see Celine Dion in Paris).

Russell looked comfortable behind the wheel, smoothly maneuvering around the course, while Antonelli took a more chaotic approach, colliding with buoys, stalling his boat, and taking a few unexpected detours. The professional drivers ultimately lost to two Bonvoy members, who posted the fastest average time.

Afterward, Antonelli and Russell headed to the Mercedes Fan Hub on Bellagio Drive, where they tested their pit-stop skills and greeted fans. Across the Strip, Williams driver Carlos Sainz returned to ARIA Resort & Casino with his Smooth Operator Dance Lounge, while Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc met fans at Bellagio’s Ferrari boutique.

Formula 1’s growing popularity has increasingly turned Grand Prix weekends into multi-day cultural events, and Las Vegas pushes that formula to its extreme.

On Friday night, the spectacle shifted from racing to rodeo. Uber and Zoox transformed MGM Grand Garden Arena into an invitation-only “Disco Rodeo” celebrating Zoox’s autonomous robotaxis joining the Uber app. Guests entered a surreal Western-meets-disco setting filled with mirrored decor before professional bull riders, trick riders, and roping performers took over a dirt arena.

Close to midnight, Grammy-winning artist Kacey Musgraves rode into the arena on horseback before performing for a crowd that included Teyana Taylor and Tiësto. Musgraves moved through songs including “Dry Spell” and “Butterflies,” turning one of Las Vegas’ biggest arenas into an unlikely combination of concert, nightclub, and rodeo.

By race day, the action returned to the Strip, where the paddock hosted a steady stream of A-list guests. Anthony Mackie, Keanu Reeves, Damson Idris, Simu Liu, and Kim Kardashian were among the famous faces spotted around the circuit, while K-pop artist REI AMI headlined the pre-race Grid Gigs.

Before Jordin Sparks sang the national anthem, 11 celebrity guests took over for the traditional drivers’ parade, navigating the 6.2-kilometer circuit in drivable Lego Formula 1 cars made from more than 28,000 bricks each. DJ Carl Cox represented Mercedes, Lisa drove for Ferrari, Gordon Ramsay took McLaren’s wheel and Terry Crews represented Cadillac. Australian DJ Fisher, driving for Red Bull, took the win.

The Las Vegas Strip Circuit itself is built for spectacle, threading 17 corners through the heart of the city and past some of its most recognizable landmarks. By Saturday night, grandstands, hotel terraces and hospitality suites were packed with fans watching Formula 1 cars flash beneath the neon lights, with the Sphere glowing over the circuit and the Strip providing a backdrop unlike any other race on the calendar.

When the lights went out, the 50-lap Las Vegas Grand Prix delivered the fast-paced drama the city had promised. Max Verstappen and George Russell repeatedly battled near the front, while Ferrari teammates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc made contact late in the race. Mercedes’ hopes of a podium faded in the closing laps, with Antonelli finishing fourth and Russell ninth.

Verstappen ultimately claimed his third Las Vegas victory, crossing the line ahead of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, who completed the podium. Actor Chris Pratt waved the checkered flag as the four-time World Champion crossed the finish line.

Official F1 Vegas merch is still available online and on sale right now for Black Friday.

The end of the race did little to slow Las Vegas down. The Backstreet Boys headlined Formula 1’s inaugural official afterparty at Sphere, carrying the celebration late into the night. The afterparty matched the city around it: energetic, entertaining and intentionally excessive, keeping the momentum going long after the final cars left the circuit.

Las Vegas marked the first stop in Formula 1’s final triple-header of 2026. Next, the grid heads to the Qatar Grand Prix before closing the season at the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, bringing another year of racing and the spectacle surrounding it to a close.

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. Amazon's early Black Friday 2026 sale is already bringing some substantial discounts on smart home devices, with savings ranging from $23 to $700 across security cameras, video doorbells, smart locks, home security systems, thermostats, and robot vacuums. Several products are more than 50% off, including indoor security cameras from Blink, Ring, and Arlo, while higher-end devices from Eufy and Roborock are seeing price cuts of hundreds of dollars.

You can also check out our other Black Friday coverage for more tech deals as the sale continues. For now, here are some of the best early Black Friday 2026 smart home deals worth checking out.

Named the best security camera of 2024 by PCMag, TP-Link’s Tapo MagCam C425 is now down to $54.99 from $89.99, making it an affordable option for keeping an eye on your driveway, backyard, or front entrance without having to run power cables. It records in 2K resolution and runs on a rechargeable battery, while support for microSD storage lets you save footage locally without paying for a cloud subscription.

Reolink’s 4K Solar Security Camera is down to $144.99 from $229.99, saving you $85. It connects over 4G LTE, so it can keep watch over a barn, vacation home, construction sites, or other areas where a regular wifi security camera won't work because there’s no home network to join. Its microSD support lets you save footage locally without a cloud subscription—you will, however, need an active cellular data plan to get the camera online.

Eufy’s SoloCam S340 is $119.99, down from $219.99, and it pairs a 3K wide-angle lens with a 2K telephoto lens, giving you a view of the whole yard and a closer look at faces or packages at the same time. The camera pans a full 360 degrees and tilts to follow people as they move, and the included solar panel keeps it charged in a sunny spot. Footage is stored on 8GB of built-in storage with no monthly fee—one of the reasons why the S340 earned an Editors’ Choice award in PCMag’s review.

Eufy’s Video Doorbell E340 is $99.99, down from $169.99, and it uses two cameras to cover your front door, with one recording visitors in 2K and the other pointing down at the doorstep to keep an eye on deliveries. It also has color night vision, a removable rechargeable battery, and 8GB of built-in storage for recording footage without a cloud subscription. You can read more about its performance in PCMag's review.

At $28, down from $79.99, the second-generation Arlo Wireless Video Doorbell 2K is one of the more affordable ways to keep an eye on your front door. Its 2K camera provides a detailed view of visitors, while the wide field of view helps capture packages left near your doorstep—making it easy to see why PCMag named it the best video doorbell of 2024.

The Blink Battery Doorbell 2K+ is down to $34.99 from $79.99. It records in 2K resolution and offers a head-to-toe view, so you can see who's at the door as well as any packages left on your doorstep. And since it runs on batteries, installation is relatively simple, especially for renters or anyone who doesn't want to deal with doorbell wiring. For more on it, check out PCMag’s review.

The Eufy Security FamiLock E34 is down to $179.99 from $279.99, saving you $100 on a smart lock that uses palm vein recognition to unlock your door, which Eufy says takes just 0.6 seconds. It can store palm data for up to 50 people locally, making it convenient for households with multiple users, while PIN codes and app-based controls give you other ways to get inside. You also get built-in wifi and compatibility with Apple Home, Alexa, Google Home, and Matter.

The Ultraloq Bolt Fingerprint smart lock is $139.99, down from $199.99, and it replaces your deadbolt with a lock you can open using a fingerprint, a keypad code, or the U Home app over built-in wifi. It can also unlock automatically as you walk up to the door, using your phone’s location. PCMag named it the best smart lock of 2024.

SimpliSafe’s DIY 8-piece Wireless Home Security System is down to $119.99 from $209.99, making it a relatively affordable starting point for securing multiple entry points around your home. The Arlo Home Security System is $142.49, down from $199.99, and this starter kit pairs a Keypad Sensor Hub with two All-in-One Sensors, each of which can be set to detect motion, open doors and windows, water leaks, and other events across eight functions. At just $15.99, down from $39.99, the Blink Mini 2K+ is one of the cheapest ways to add indoor monitoring to your smart home. This compact plug-in camera records in 2K resolution, and also supports motion alerts, two-way audio, and Alexa integration. PCMag has a review of the Blink Mini 2K+.

Arlo’s Essential Pan Tilt Indoor Cam 2K is $18.99, down from $49.99, and it’s part of the lineup Arlo released in 2025, with a motorized head that rotates a full 360 degrees and tilts 180 degrees so one camera can cover an entire room. This PCMag review goes into more detail on how it performs.

The Sensi Smart Thermostat ST55 is currently $79, down from $129.99, and is a good option for anyone looking to control their home's heating and cooling from a phone—it lets you create schedules, adjust temperatures remotely, and use geofencing to make changes based on whether you're home or away. It also works with several popular smart home platforms, including Alexa, Google Assistant, and Samsung SmartThings, plus Apple HomeKit when a C-wire is connected, notes this PCMag review.

It works with Alexa to let you adjust temperatures through voice commands or the Alexa app, where you can also set schedules and automate temperature changes based on your routines. For more on its cleaning performance, check out PCMag’s review.

#3301. iOS 27 lets you use two iPhones with the same phone number

9to5Mac is brought to you by Tello Mobile. Switching to Tello Mobile can bring the cost of your plan down to as little as $5 a month, or an unlimited plan for just $25 a month, all on America’s largest 5G network. See all of the available plans at tello.com.

Among iOS 27’s many new features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

With iOS 27, Apple introduces big AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting new features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the update also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

After iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

Most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

I feel like I’m exactly who this feature was made for. After years of running dual SIM, I now have a personal line on my Duo and work line on an 18 Pro. Going out with friends, family, etc, I’d love to bring one phone again while bringing both numbers with me, but keeping work system access to a specific, separate device. Only current problem is waiting for Verizon to activate the feature and then see if it actually works well.

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”

So far carrier support is limited (here’s the latest list), but Apple plans to expand iPhone Handoff to more carriers soon.

Do you have a need to use the same phone number on multiple iPhones? For what reason? Let us know in the comments.

#3300. Everything We Know About Gina Prince-Bythewood’s ‘Children Of Blood And Bone’ Movie So Far

As summer draws to a close, the theatrical release of Children of Blood and Bone draws nearer.

The film adaptation of Tomi Adeyemi’s YA fantasy is directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, and it stars quite a stacked cast of actors and characters.

For everything we know about the Children of Blood and Bone movie, read on.

When will Gina Prince-Bythewood’s Children of Blood and Bone come out?

The film will arrive in theaters January 15, 2027 as one of the first highly anticipated releases of the new year.

Who is in the cast of the Children of Blood and Bone movie? Watch on Deadline

Thuso Mbedu, who worked with both director Prince-Bythewood and costar Viola Davis on The Woman King (2022), will star as the main character Zelie. Amandla Stenberg (The Hate U Give, The Acolyte) will portray Amari. Damson Idris (F1, Snowfall) will play Inan. Tosin Cole (Supacell) will portray Tzain.

Davis will portray Mama Agba. Cynthia Erivo (Wicked) will portray Admiral Kaea. Idris Elba (Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw) will play Lekan. Lashana Lynch (Bob Marley: One Love) plays Jumoke, and Chiwetel Ejiofor (12 Years a Slave) plays King Saran. Regina King (Shirley) will appear as Queen Nehanda. Diaana Babnicova will portray Folake and Buuky Bakray will portray Binta.

Saniyya Sidney (Fences), Zackary Momoh (Harriet), Richard Mofe-Damijo (Namaste Wahala), Ayra Starr, Pamilerin Ayodeji (Mikolo), Shamz Garuba (Crime and Justice Lagos), Kola Bodunde (Shadow) and Temi Fagbenle rounded out the cast later on. Ayodeji and Garuba were cast through an open casting call in Nigeria.

Is there a trailer for the Children of Blood and Bone movie?

Yes, a trailer was released in late July, introducing the cast and their characters as Orïsha faces a battle for its magic. Another trailer was released in early November along with artists who have contributed songs to the film.

RELATED: Gina Prince-Bythewood’s ‘Children Of Blood And Bone’ Trailer Glimpses Thuso Mbedu’s Quest To Restore Magic To Orïsha

What is Children of Blood and Bone about?

The first novel in the Legacy of Orïsha trilogy chronicles Zelie’s journey to restore the intrinsic magic to the land after King Saran made a move to purge it, seeing it as a threat and unnatural. Drawning on African mythology, the fantasy setting contains groups of humans that practice magic known as Maji. The Maji divine certain elements, and thus are known by the specific powers they wield, from water workers beckoning tides to those like Zelie’s mother Jumoke, who can summon souls.

Zelie and her brother team up with the son and daughter of King Saran. Prince Inan (Idris) has doubts about taking on his father’s crown and following King Saran’s example directly.

What artists will have music in the upcoming Children of Blood and Bone movie?

Tems serves as the soundtrack executive producer, and has contributed “African Love Song” which is featured in the film’s second trailer. Beyoncé’s “Energy (feat. Beam)” featured in the first trailer. Guest features on the soundtrack include:

Is Tomi Adeyemi involved in the movie adaptation of Children of Blood and Bone?

Adeyemi co-wrote the screenplay with Prince-Bythewood. She has expressed that she won’t watch the film, and she posted a video on Instagram explaining her experience on set.

RELATED: ‘Children of Blood & Bone’ Author Tomi Adeyemi “Will Not Watch” Film Adaptation: “It’s Been Painful”

Are there more Children of Blood and Bone books? Will there be more movies?

Yes, the book gave way to a trilogy. Following Children of Blood and Bone‘s publish date in 2018, Children of Virtue and Vengeance arrived in 2019, and Children of Anguish and Anarchy arrived in 2024.

There are currently no plans to adapt the next two books in the series into films.

Adeyemi has The Siren coming out at the end of September.

#3298. Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

According to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

If you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

#3295. How to Watch F1 Like a Pro, According to McLaren Drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

As the 2026 F1 season made its final U.S. stop of the year, Las Vegas once again turned its neon-lit streets into an impressive, 17-turn race that wound its way through The Strip, with drivers whizzing past the city’s most iconic landmarks. On Sunday, Max Verstappen took home the checkered flag at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix after a nail-biting finish, with McLaren’s Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri posting a double-podium finish to complete the top three.

With F1’s growing prominence in the U.S., new fans continue to enter the high-speed world of racing. But while the rules of Formula 1 seem simple enough — the first car to pass the checkered flag after 50-odd laps, wins — it does take some time to truly understand the complexities of the sport.

Rolling Stone sat down with McLaren drivers Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix to glean some tips on how new fans can optimize their viewing experience.

Norris advises the audience to watch onboard videos and listen to the commentators who make the race more understandable. “When you then see the onboard cameras in the driver’s eye [line], I think it looks a lot more realistic [since] that is what I’m seeing with my head,” he says, “So I think that gives a much better experience. The more that they can do that, and get the sensation of speed, the easier it will be for people to understand.”

And while new viewers might only focus on the leaderboard, Piastri begs to differ. “I think the first thing about Formula 1 is not everyone’s car is the same, so I think just because some people aren’t winning, it doesn’t necessarily mean that they’re worse than the people that are winning,” he says. “Oftentimes the racing in the midfield can sometimes be more entertaining than the racing at the front.”

The drivers both say that strategy shifts within varying climate conditions, tire compounds and their impact to performance and longevity, and the car’s on-track behavior are just a few of the factors being considered on the sidelines during every race.

As part of their preparation, the team reviews prior races of the current season, as well as footage of the same track last year to see any learnings that could apply. Norris emphasizes how the addition of new cameras showing extra angles on the track can help the driver’s pre-race POV while adding to the immersive fan experience.

T-Mobile, F1’s regional 5G innovation partner, supports this by (literally) taking connectivity to new heights, with more than 20 5G-connected cameras that supply additional angles and track views. With its partnership with Apple TV, more angles are made available to the customer, in addition to a private 5G network to ensure reliable connectivity for broadcast feeds.

“We saw an opportunity with the technology-forward nature of the sport to be able to come in and look at how could we provide network solutions that are actually making the experience better,” offers Amy Azzi, VP of Sponsorships and Events at T-Mobile.

Azzi highlights the “additional broadcast views and angles, using our connectivity, and devices that are able to capture those angles and bring them into a more functional broadcast or into the app, which allow more opportunities for fans to engage.”

For fans who can’t watch the races live, the network giant recently launched T-Mix, where customers can mix and match benefits and entertainment options every three months, including streamers like Apple TV, home of the F1 U.S. broadcast, alongside other premier streamers, travel partners, and music providers.

At the end of the day, the McLaren duo’s most important connections are to their supporters. Piastri says he’s collected his fair share of fan gifts this year, shouting out a glitter-covered cowboy hat in his helmet design, to a hardcover book with special fan messages. “Hearing some some people’s stories and how coming to an F1 race is literally their life dream, and being able to to help them kind of fulfill that dream is is really cool,” he says.

Norris emphasizes that fans are the most important thing in their sport. To wit: the driver kicked off race week by doing an exclusive meet-and-greet at T-Mobile’s Las Vegas Signature Store, where fans got to experience an F1 simulator and other racing-inspired activations while getting up close and personal to one of the sports biggest stars.

“The fans are the reason our sport is what it is, and you don’t just say it because you have to,” he says. “What I love to do is the driving [but] the bonus I get out of it is I have people traveling around the world, supporting me, cheering me on, wanting me to do well. I feel like I need to go out and perform well for them to make it feel like their trip was worth it.”

T-Mobile has been part of the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix since its inaugural race in 2023, and the mobile carrier once again brought its members-only Club Magenta viewing experience to the track this year, while also sponsoring performances from artists like Ja Rule, Gorgon City and Natasha Bedingfield on the T-Mobile Stage. Saturday culminated with the first-ever official post-race show with the Backstreet Boys at Sphere.

#3294. You Can Get One of These Pocket E-Readers for As Little As $55 Before Black Friday

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a big discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing new firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

#3293. ESR Black Friday gift guide: Premium accessories for iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, iPad, AirPods, and Apple Watch

If you picked up a new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo this fall, or you’re shopping for someone with an iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch, there’s a good chance you’ve been holding out on purchasing accessories until all of the Black Friday deals started. We’ve got you covered with some great deals on premium accessories for nearly every Apple device on your list.

ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile. Here’s a look at what’s included in ESR’s Black Friday lineup and who each one is for.

If someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right. As we’ve seen with Android foldables, you’re protecting two halves, a hinge, and a phone that changes shape throughout the day as you use it, all without adding bulk to a device people bought because it folds thin. ESR has two options for iPhone Duo owners, and the choice mostly comes down to the look you want to achieve.

The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand is your choice if you want to show off your iPhone Duo’s colors. It combines a rigid polycarbonate and acrylic back with a softer TPU frame. The rigid back keeps the case from flexing and lets the iPhone Duo’s design show through, while the flexible frame absorbs the shock if you drop it (please don’t).

The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand is perfect for those who want a more premium look for their iPhone Duo. It’s made from organic silicone leather with a soft, skin-friendly feel and a stain-resistant finish. If you’ve ever used a light-colored leather case before, you know it usually shows every stain and smudge it comes across, but ESR built the Atelier to resist daily wear and wipe clean.

Both cases share ESR’s Flex Stand, and it’s one of the most innovative and versatile parts of the lineup. It’s a 180-degree rotating stand made from zinc alloy, so it holds its shape even after months of propping up your iPhone. A precision hinge with damping control lets it open smoothly and lock at the angle you choose, whether the iPhone Duo is folded or unfolded, and ESR says it has passed 3,000 open-and-close tests. In real life, that means propping the iPhone Duo open on a desk for a video call or on an airplane tray table for a movie, then using the stand as a grip when you’re holding it.

Both cases add extra hinge protection and raised edges where a foldable is most exposed. If you follow our MagSafe Monday column, you know magnetic strength really matters for MagSafe wallets, car mounts, etc. The Classic Hybrid has 1,500g of magnetic hold, and the Atelier has 1,400g.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case for iPhone Duo is 15% off.

The same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

On these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

Protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

Why it matters: ESR says the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing shows up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Installation is the part most people dread on a brand-new iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

Holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. An extra USB-C port lets a second device charge simultaneously. 9to5Mac’s Michael Burkhardt went hands-on with the Xtend 45W earlier this month and said it’s an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go.

It’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR says it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

For the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

For a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

The trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the new M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

Have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

When the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR says the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

The result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Both cases also have 260g of magnetic strength, so they snap onto MagSafe chargers, Apple Watch chargers, and MagSafe batteries if you need to charge your AirPods. Again, it’s extremely strong, but extremely easy to unlock with one hand.

The ESR Cyber FlickLock Magnetic Case is extremely durable and has a clip hook, so you can hang your AirPods on a backpack while hiking or cycling. The ESR Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Case brings the same lock in a range of vibrant colors with a carrying lanyard, so you can wear your AirPods on your wrist or attach them to a bag. Both cases come in versions for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 and 1, and AirPods 5 and 4. No matter which AirPods you or your loved one have, this is the case everyone will love.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

The ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. It fits 44mm, 45mm, 46mm, and 49mm models across Apple Watch Ultra 1 through 4, Series 4 through 12, and SE 1 through 3, and it comes in several colors to match your outfit or your mood that day.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Equinox Watch Band is 20% off.

The best gifts are the ones that get used every day, and accessories are the part of the Apple experience people live with the most. A case that props up a foldable, a screen protector made with Corning glass, a charger with a built-in cable, and an AirPods case that stays closed even when dropped check all the boxes. ESR truly makes something for everyone and is one of the most trusted names in the Apple accessories ecosystem.

ESR built its Black Friday lineup around the whole Apple ecosystem, from the new iPhone Duo to iPad, AirPods, and even a great Apple Watch band, with premium materials and versatile designs that are durable, functional, and great-looking. ESR’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals run on Amazon from November 19 through November 30 (the Xtend 45W runs through December 1), with discounts of up to 37%!

Be sure to follow ESR on X and Facebook to keep up with all of its latest products, deals, and more.

#3292. These Are the Best Early Black Friday 2026 Deals on DeWalt Tools

Becca Lewis is home maintenance writer who aims to foster confidence in and inspire DIY enthusiasts at all skill levels.

Becca attended Southern Connecticut State University, where she studied technical theater and design. She has a background in carpentry and fabrication and has worked in specialty shops, using a wide variety of tools and materials, for more than 20 years.

Becca has also written for Angi, where she specializes in creating guides for DIY, home maintenance, and renovations, and she indulges her love of sci-fi and fantasy by writing about entertainment and science for Giant Freakin Robot. She serves on the board of the Good Junk Sanctuary in Portland, Oregon, focusing on community engagement in the DIY and reuse space.

If you need some new tools for your holiday DIY projects, or if you have a DIYer on your list, Black Friday deals are one of the best ways to save money on tools. DeWalt has been making cordless tools for over 30 years, and it has a reputation for making durable, reliable tools. Here are the best early Black Friday deals on DeWalt cordless tools.

A good quality drill and driver is the foundation of a home tool set because they allow you to drive screws and bolts and drill pilot holes for basic projects like putting up shelves, as well as more advanced woodworking and maintenance tasks.

The DeWalt 20-volt MAX drill and driver set is on sale on Amazon for $129, 46% off its regular price. The set comes with a drill, an impact driver, two 1.5-amp-hour batteries, a charger, and a tool bag. This is a good starter set because it has everything you need to use it right out of the box.

The DeWalt 20-volt compact drill is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 45% off its usual price. It comes with a 20-volt, 2-amp-hour battery and a charger. This is the first basic cordless tool you need for most DIY home maintenance.

The DeWalt 20-volt compact impact driver is on sale at Home Depot for $99, 45% off its usual price. It comes with a 2-amp-hour battery and a charger. This is a good tool for an expanding home tool set, allowing you to drive screws and bolts into tougher materials with less effort.

Saws and trimming tools are a key part of a compact tool set if you plan to cut and shape your materials. They can be useful for DIY projects from fence repair to installing custom trim.

The DeWalt 60-volt Flex 7 ¼-inch circular saw is on sale at Home Depot for $299, 52% off its regular price. This saw comes with a 60-20-volt Flex 12-amp-hour battery. You’ll need a charger for the high-capacity battery. This is a good saw for working farther away from a power source because the battery is designed for longer run-time between charges.

The DeWalt 20-volt MAX cordless jigsaw and the DeWalt 20-volt MAX cordless router are on sale at Home Depot for $199 at Home Depot, 60% off its usual price. They come with a 4-amp-hour battery, a 6-amp-hour battery, and a charger. These are woodworking tools that can be used to shape trim and make specialty cuts.

The DeWalt 60-volt Flex compact cordless angle grinder is on sale at Home Depot for $299, 51% off its typical price. This tool comes with a 20-60-volt battery. You’ll need a charger for the high-capacity battery. This is a good tool for metalworking or for grinding off screw and nail tips if they poke through your material.

The DeWalt 20-volt oscillating multi-tool set is on sale for $99, 50% off its regular price. This set comes with the oscillating multitool, a 2-amp-hour battery, and sanding attachment and accessory wrench, and four sheets of sandpaper. This is a versatile tool that can be used for cutting and finishing projects.

Batteries are one of the most expensive parts of a cordless tool set, and having a few extras so you can always have a fresh battery on the charger to swap out helps keep your DIY projects moving.

A two-pack of DeWalt 20-volt MAX 2-amp-hour batteries is on sale at Home Depot for $79, 53% off its regular price.

A set of two DeWalt 20-volt MAX batteries and two 20-volt MAX 4-amp-hour batteries is on sale for $199, 45% off its typical price.

The best early deals on tools right now are at Home Depot, where you can get up to 65% off on select Milwaukee tools, 50% off on DeWalt tools, and 30% off on Ryobi tools. They also have several offers for over 50% off on hand tools.

Yes, Home Depot has already launched its early Black Friday deals, offering deep discounts on major brands of cordless power tools. They also update their sales page on Thanksgiving Day and include Black Friday in-store-only doorbusters as part of their seasonal sales.

Home Depot and Lowe’s often compete with each other for seasonal sales, so it’s always a good idea to check both sites before buying. Right now, Home Depot has the best deals on DeWalt and Milwaukee cordless tool sets, but Lowe’s has a better deal on Craftsman hand tool sets.

The best prices of the year on tools are during the holidays in November and December. This is because of the holiday shopping push, as well as making space for new tools that come out in the spring. The second-best time to buy tools is in May and June during Father’s Day sales.

For most home tool sets, Ryobi is a solid, durable, and versatile brand. If you plan to use your tools occasionally for home maintenance, this is the best bang for your buck. For daily use or for larger DIY projects, DeWalt tends to be the next best option. These tools have more robust chargers and tend to stand up to more rigorous use than Ryobi tools.

New York Knicks star OG Anunoby made headlines during the team’s NBA championship run last season when it was revealed that he wears Skechers basketball shoes on the court. Now, the Knicks guard and power forward is teaming up with the footwear brand on a new pair of sneakers that pay tribute to the city and team he helped bring a trophy to.

Skechers Basketball and Anunoby have just dropped the SKX Nexus “NYC Blue,” a limited-edition pair of sneakers released in the same colorway worn by OG during his now-legendary game-winning tip-in that helped propel New York to an NBA Championship.

The “NYC Blue” colorway pays tribute to the shade of blue seen in the Knicks’ uniforms, while orange laces and accents complete the official team colors.

The shoes themselves feature a breathable and flexible mesh upper, enhanced ankle support, 5GEN midsole cushioning with torsion plate, and a grippy Goodyear outsole for traction on the court. OG’s logo is seen on the sockliner and embroidered on the tongue, with his signature on the heel for an extra personalized touch.

Skechers says these are shoes designed to boost performance, with lightweight materials, a supportive silhouette, an cushy insole for added comfort, and a “strategically-designed forefoot traction pattern” for precise quick cuts.

The limited-edition sneakers ship in a custom-designed box and come with a set of collectible enamel pins with Knicks motifs. Skechers has the unisex basketball shoes available in men’s sizes 4 to 17.

While Anunoby’s Player Edition basketball shoe is now available to shop online at Skechers.com, it’s been a long time coming — the SKX Nexus NYC Blue was first announced for pre-orders in June.

In press materials, Skechers says “This release marks a historic milestone, representing the brand’s first-ever championship win and a defining moment in Skechers Basketball’s rapid rise in the performance space.”

Anunoby signed a multi-year footwear and apparel endorsement deal with Skechers in July 2025.
